lesson.subject: literacy
lesson.title: Edit Like a Pro
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 5, Session 3
lesson.footer: Persuasive Writing | Year 5/6 Literacy | Week 5 Session 3

plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LA09 commas to mark prepositional phrases and apostrophes for multiple possession; VC2E5LY11 editing using agreed criteria; VC2E5LY03 and LY04 spelling
plan.shape: error race, two quick rules, then a slow edit: commas after an opening where or when phrase, apostrophes for one or many owners, then a read-aloud CUPS edit of their own draft
plan.criticalFeature: read it aloud, slowly, once for each check: the pause tells you the comma, the owner tells you the apostrophe
decisionPoints: the choice check: the correct sentence
the exit board: two fixes in a new sentence
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Clean writing lets every move land.
plan.catchUp: Missed the drafting week? Edit any paragraph you have; the rules work on any writing.

studentTools: Writing books with the revised draft
A different coloured pencil for edits
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: CUPS: Capitals, Usage, Punctuation, Spelling. One read-aloud per letter.
Where or when phrase first? Comma after it.

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn: add commas, write possessives, spot the correct sentence, then log your CUPS edits.
resources.title: Edit Like a Pro
resources.subtitle: Read it aloud, slowly, once for each check.

steps: Find the where or when phrase at the start
Read it aloud: hear the pause?
Add a comma at the pause

items.prompt: Rewrite each sentence with the comma in the right place.
rows: Across the bay the ice cracked.
During summer the bears go hungry.
Behind our school a creek runs.
At the zoo the bear paced.
In the morning the canteen opens.
answers: Across the bay the ice cracked.
Across the bay, the ice cracked.
During summer the bears go hungry.
During summer, the bears go hungry.
Behind our school a creek runs.
Behind our school, a creek runs.
At the zoo the bear paced.
At the zoo, the bear paced.
In the morning the canteen opens.
In the morning, the canteen opens.

steps: One: 's. Many ending in s: s'.

items.prompt: Write each one with an apostrophe.

example.prompt: Which is right? In winter the ice grows. / In winter, the ice grows.
steps: Is there a comma after it?

options: Near the shore the walruses' tusks shone.
Near the shore, the walruses' tusks shone.
Near the shore, the walrus's' tusks shone.
items.explain: Comma after the opening phrase; walruses' for many walruses.

items.prompt: Noah edited this sentence. Find two mistakes and fix them.
work: On the ice the bear's cubs (two bears) played.
items.answer: Comma after On the ice; the bears' cubs for two bears. Fix: On the ice, the bears' cubs played.

steps: Read aloud once for each letter
example.answer: P: added a comma after In the Arctic.

items.prompt: Edit your draft. Log one fix for each CUPS check.
answers: a word that now makes sense

resources.subtitle: Professional editors catch everything.

example.prompt: in the arctic the bears den melts
example.answer: In the Arctic, the bear's den melts.

items.prompt: This paragraph has eight errors. Find and fix them all.
work: across the arctic the polar bears homes are melting. scientists say the ice is shrinking every year and their worried.
In the summer the bears cubs go hungry.
items.answer: Across, Arctic, comma after Arctic, bears' homes, Scientists, they're, comma after summer, bears' cubs.

steps: Start with a where or when phrase
example.answer: Around the world, scientists' warnings grow louder.

items.prompt: Write three sentences about your issue. Each starts with a where or when phrase, and one uses a plural possessive.
items.answer: Three correct sentences with commas after the opening phrases and one plural possessive.

items.prompt: Write each one with an apostrophe.
items.hint: The first one is done for you.

example.prompt: in the arctic the ice melts

resources.label: Persuasion Crossword
resources.description: Fun activity: a crossword of the unit's persuasion words. Early finishers, or a five-minute warm-up next session.
resources.title: Persuasion Crossword
resources.subtitle: Every answer is a word from our persuasive writing unit.

words.clue: A question fair people could disagree about
How one person sees an issue because of who they are
How sure a word makes an idea sound
Chosen to make the reader feel
Facts, numbers or expert words that prove a claim
The people you are trying to persuade
Make it sound bigger than it really is
An opening line that grabs the reader
A word pattern used on purpose to persuade
A short, catchy line people remember
A sneak peek at the reasons coming
Words that paint a picture in your mind
Change your writing to make it stronger

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: today we polish our writing until nothing distracts the reader.

Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension and the Persuasion Crossword for early finishers, and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. A second coloured pencil for edits; dictionaries on tables.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to edit our writing so nothing distracts the reader.
successCriteria: I can check my writing for capitals, usage, punctuation and spelling.
I can use commas after opening phrases and apostrophes for one or many owners.
I can edit my own draft by reading it aloud, once for each check.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Editors make sure nothing gets between the reader and your message.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch. Retrieves Term 3 Week 1 prepositional phrases.

slides.title: Error race!
lines: in the arctic the bears den is melting and there food is dissapearing
How many mistakes can you find in 60 seconds?

notes.answer: six: In, Arctic, comma after Arctic, bears', their, disappearing
beats: SAY: One sentence. Lots of mistakes.
Sixty seconds. How many can you find?
ASK: Write the number of mistakes you found.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4 to 6
ASK: Tell your partner the one you think most people missed.
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: the comma after Arctic; bears'
SAY: Today you hunt like this through your own draft.
trap: Fix: say there are capitals and punctuation hiding too.
notes.prep: Low-coupling, game-style launch. Six errors. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: To fix the mistakes so nothing distracts the reader.
slides.example: Disapearing becomes disappearing. That is editing.

notes.answer: to fix the mistakes so nothing distracts the reader
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Edit. Say it with me. Edit.
SAY: To fix the mistakes so nothing distracts the reader.
SAY: Disapearing becomes disappearing. That is editing.
ASK: What is the difference between revising and editing?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: revising makes it stronger; editing makes it correct
trap: thinking editing means rewriting whole paragraphs.
Fix: say editing changes letters and marks, not ideas.
notes.prep: Edit is the partner word to Session 2's revise.

slides.title: Comma after where or when
lines: In the Arctic the ice is melting.
In the Arctic, the ice is melting.
Where or when phrase first? Comma after it.

notes.answer: a where or when phrase at the start gets a comma after it
beats: POINT to the first sentence.
SAY: In the Arctic tells me where. It's at the front.
READ it aloud with a pause.
SAY: In the Arctic... pause... the ice is melting. The pause is where my comma goes.
SAY: Some of you may remember these from Term 3.
At the front, they get a comma.
ASK: During summer the bears go hungry. Where is the comma?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: after summer
trap: putting the comma after the first word: In, the Arctic.
Fix: student reads the whole phrase aloud and pauses at its end.
notes.stretch: Find a sentence in your draft that would be stronger starting with a where phrase.
notes.help: Read it aloud and clap at the pause.
notes.prep: The model for rule 1 (VC2E5LA09). Retrieval of Term 3 Week 1 prepositional phrases.

slides.title: Comma or not?
slides.pivot: read it aloud together and clap at the pause
slides.followUp: cold call one board: where is the phrase?

items.text: Under the ice seals hide from bears.
items.answer: Under the ice, seals hide from bears.

items.text: After school we walk the dog.
items.answer: After school, we walk the dog.

items.text: We walk the dog after school.
items.answer: No comma needed: the phrase is at the end.
items.say: No comma. The phrase is at the end, not the start. Tick or fix.

items.text: Across the frozen sea the bear walked for days.
items.answer: Across the frozen sea, the bear walked for days.

say: Rewrite each sentence with a comma if it needs one.
trap: adding a comma to every sentence.
Fix: ask is the where or when phrase at the START? Student checks.
notes.stretch: Move the phrase to the end of each sentence and drop the comma.
notes.help: Underline the where or when words first.
notes.prep: Guided practice including the near-miss: the phrase at the end needs no comma. SC2.

notes.answer: one owner 's; many owners ending in s add '; plurals without s add 's
beats: POINT to one bear.
SAY: One bear owns the den. Bear, apostrophe, s.
POINT to many bears.
SAY: Two bears share a den.
Bears already ends in s, so the apostrophe goes after it.
POINT to children.
SAY: Children is already plural, with no s. So children, apostrophe, s.
ASK: The ideas of the people. Write it.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: the people's ideas
trap: Fix: student asks does the plural already end in s? Children doesn't, so 's.
notes.stretch: Explain why the bears' den and the bear's den mean different things.
notes.help: Count the owners first: one or many?
notes.prep: The model for rule 2: apostrophes for multiple possession, regular and irregular (VC2E5LA09).

slides.title: Whose is it?
slides.pivot: count the owners together, then check for an s
slides.followUp: cold call one board: one owner or many?

items.say: Women has no s, so apostrophe s. Tick or fix.

say: Write each one with an apostrophe.
trap: putting the apostrophe after the s every time.
Fix: student counts owners, then checks the plural.
notes.stretch: Write a sentence using two of them.
notes.help: Use the chart on the slide before.
notes.prep: Guided practice on regular and irregular plurals. SC2.

options.text: Along the beach the seals' pups slept.
options.misconception: misses the comma after the opening phrase

options.text: Along the beach, the seals' pups slept.
Along the beach, the seal's' pups slept.
options.misconception: confused about where the apostrophe goes for many owners

notes.answer: B - comma after the phrase, seals' for many seals
beats: SAY: Check two things: the comma and the apostrophe.
ASK: Which sentence is correct?
15 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: why seals' and not seal's?
Less -> read each aloud with the pause, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. A comma at the pause, and seals' because many seals own the pups.
trap: pointing to A because the apostrophe is right.
Fix: read it aloud; ask where do you pause?
notes.prep: Decision point before editing drafts. Under 80% means a second run of each rule on the board.

slides.title: Edit your draft
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Then edit your draft in a new colour: read it aloud once for each CUPS check.

notes.answer: a draft edited in colour, with a CUPS log
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Edits go in a new colour. Read your draft aloud, quietly, once for each letter.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Point to one sentence: read it to me. Where's the pause?
ASK: Which CUPS check are you up to?
1 for C, 2 for U, 3 for P, 4 for S.
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2 or more by halfway
trap: Fix: student reads aloud, finger under each word.
notes.stretch: Extension: catch eight errors, then write sentences using today's rules. Then the crossword.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a first answer done, a short check.
notes.prep: Independent editing of their own drafts. Final copies are written next session. SC2 and SC3.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in a CUPS log, then the draft edited in colour

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Beside the river the farmers paddocks were flooded.
Rewrite it correctly. There are two fixes.

notes.answer: Beside the river, the farmers' paddocks were flooded.
beats: SAY: A new sentence. Two fixes needed.
ASK: Rewrite the sentence correctly.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: comma after river; farmers' (many farmers)
RECORD who misses the comma or writes farmer's. Small group before Publish Day.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new sentence. Farmer's is acceptable only if the student says one farmer; record either way.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner your most common mistake, and how you'll catch it.

notes.answer: open - I forget commas after opening phrases; I'll read aloud and pause
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can edit your own writing?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: Tell your partner your most common mistake, and how you'll catch it.
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: I forget commas after opening phrases; I'll read aloud and pause
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit boards. SC2.
